step_by_step_reasoning:
Step-by-step reasoning and utility of knowledge-base functions:

1) Determine available knowledge-base functions: none were provided in the environment (the <functions> list is empty). Therefore no external helper functions are available or used; all actions must use Playwright page methods directly.

2) Navigation to Manage Products: using a relative goto is appropriate and required by the prompt. This avoids clicking a top-level Catalog link that might navigate unexpectedly and keeps the click actions more deterministic.

3) Clicking Add Product: use page.get_by_role("button", name="Add Product") as the primary accessible selector. If not present, try a link or an "Add" button. Using get_by_role keeps to the Accessibility Tree-centric selector requirement.

4) Product type/attribute set step: some Magento installs require choosing product type (Simple Product). If a radio labeled "Simple Product" exists, check it with the radio-specific .check() method.

5) Continue: click the Continue button using get_by_role. Wait for networkidle after clicking as the product edit page loads.

6) Fill product fields: use page.get_by_label("Name") and page.get_by_label("Price").fill(...) rather than page.fill with CSS selectors, to satisfy the constraint to use accessibility-based filling.
   - Try multiple plausible label strings ("Name", "Product Name" and for price "Price", "Price (Excl. Tax)") to be robust to minor UI differences.

7) Status: attempt to set Status to Enabled using get_by_label("Status").select_option(label="Enabled"). If Status is presented as radios, check the Enabled radio.

8) Attributes (Size, Color): prefer get_by_label("Size").select_option(label="S") and get_by_label("Color").select_option(label="Blue"). If the control is implemented as radios, fall back to checking the appropriate radio via get_by_role("radio", name=...). All interactions use accessibility-aware methods.

9) Inventory section: open the Inventory tab using get_by_role("link", name="Inventory"), or as a tab/button if needed. Waiting briefly for content to appear.

10) Qty and Stock Availability: fill Qty via get_by_label("Qty") or get_by_label("Quantity"). For stock availability, try select_option on get_by_label("Stock Availability") or check a radio/checkbox labeled "In Stock". Again, all selectors are accessibility-centric.

11) Save: use get_by_role("button", name="Save").click() as the final action because it will likely navigate or reload the page. If Save is not present, fallback to "Save and Continue Edit".

Notes about knowledge-base functions: none exist in the provided <functions> section, so no calls were made to external helper functions. All actions use Playwright page methods and strictly use accessibility-oriented selectors (get_by_role, get_by_label) and .select_option/.check/.fill methods as appropriate.
